- public static Evaluator parse(String query)

- Evaluator parse() (package-private)

- private void byClass()

- private void byAttribute()

- private void indexGreaterThan()

- private void indexEquals()

- private void cssNthChild(boolean backwards, boolean ofType)

- private int consumeIndex()

- private void has()

- private void contains(boolean own)

- private void containsData()

- private void matches(boolean own)

- private void not()

But only parse is public.

We can write tests that verify that parse returns appropriate Evaluator types for given selectors. Need to import org.jsoup.select.* and maybe use instance checks.

Edge cases: null query? The code doesn't handle null, TokenQueue may throw NPE. Should test that parse throws SelectorParseException for invalid selectors, e.g., empty string, unknown token, malformed attribute, missing closing parenthesis, etc.

Also test combinator handling: multiple selectors with comma, >, +, ~, space.

Test attribute selectors with operators, e.g., [attr], [^attr], [attr=val], [attr!=val], [attr^=val], [attr$=val], [attr*=val], [attr~=regex].

Test pseudo selectors: :lt(3), :gt(2), :eq(1), :nth-child(2n+1), :first-child, etc.

Test :not(...)

Also test namespace handling: "*|tag", "ns|tag" etc.

Will need to assert that the Evaluator is instance of certain classes, and maybe evaluate its toString? But Evaluator may not have accessible properties. We can just assert class type.

We'll need to import org.junit.Test, org.junit.Assert.*.

Also need to handle Selector.SelectorParseException.

We need to write a test class QueryParserTest with many @Test methods.

Let's propose a series of test methods covering each.

We'll need to reference internal classes: Evaluator, StructuralEvaluator, CombiningEvaluator, etc. Those are package-private classes within org.jsoup.select, but accessible within same package. Our test class should be in same package org.jsoup.select to access package-private methods? But parse returns Evaluator which is public. The concrete evaluator classes are probably public static inner classes? Actually Evaluator is an interface in org.jsoup.select, with many static subclasses like Evaluator.Id, .Class, .Tag etc. They are public static classes inside Evaluator? In jsoup they are public static classes inside Evaluator. So we can reference them.

Thus test can be in same package org.jsoup.select.

We'll create tests:

- testParseSimpleTag: "div" returns Evaluator.Tag

- testParseId: "#myId" returns Evaluator.Id

- testParseClass: ".myClass" returns Evaluator.Class

- testParseAllElements: "*" returns Evaluator.AllElements

- testParseAttributeExists: "[href]" returns Evaluator.Attribute

- testParseAttributeEquals: "[href=example.com]" returns Evaluator.AttributeWithValue

- testParseAttributeNotEquals: "[href!=example.com]" returns Evaluator.AttributeWithValueNot

- testParseAttributeStartsWith: "[href^=http]" returns Evaluator.AttributeWithValueStarting

- testParseAttributeEndsWith: "[href$=.com]" returns Evaluator.AttributeWithValueEnding

- testParseAttributeContains: "[href*=example]" returns Evaluator.AttributeWithValueContaining

- testParseAttributeRegex: "[href~=^https?://]" returns Evaluator.AttributeWithValueMatching

- testParsePseudoLt: ":lt(3)" returns Evaluator.IndexLessThan

- testParsePseudoGt: ":gt(1)" returns Evaluator.IndexGreaterThan

- testParsePseudoEq: ":eq(2)" returns Evaluator.IndexEquals

- testParsePseudoNthChild: ":nth-child(2n+1)" returns Evaluator.IsNthChild

- testParsePseudoFirstChild: ":first-child" returns Evaluator.IsFirstChild

- testParsePseudoLastChild: ":last-child" returns Evaluator.IsLastChild

- testParsePseudoOnlyChild: ":only-child" returns Evaluator.IsOnlyChild

- testParsePseudoEmpty: ":empty" returns Evaluator.IsEmpty

- testParsePseudoRoot: ":root" returns Evaluator.IsRoot

- testParsePseudoHas: "div:has(p)" returns StructuralEvaluator.Has

- testParsePseudoContains: "p:contains(text)" returns Evaluator.ContainsText

- testParsePseudoContainsOwn: "p:containsOwn(text)" returns Evaluator.ContainsOwnText

- testParsePseudoContainsData: "p:containsData(data)" returns Evaluator.ContainsData

- testParsePseudoMatches: "p:matches(\\d+)" returns Evaluator.Matches

- testParsePseudoMatchesOwn: "p:matchesOwn(\\d+)" returns Evaluator.MatchesOwn

- testParseNot: "div:not(.class)" returns StructuralEvaluator.Not

- testParseCombinatorChild: "div > p" returns CombiningEvaluator.And with StructuralEvaluator.ImmediateParent

- testParseCombinatorDescendant: "div p" returns CombiningEvaluator.And with StructuralEvaluator.Parent

- testParseCombinatorAdjacentSibling: "div + p" returns CombiningEvaluator.And with StructuralEvaluator.ImmediatePreviousSibling

- testParseCombinatorGeneralSibling: "div ~ p" returns CombiningEvaluator.And with StructuralEvaluator.PreviousSibling

- testParseGroupComma: "div, p" returns CombiningEvaluator.Or

- testParseNamespaceWildcard: "*|div" returns CombiningEvaluator.Or (Tag plus TagEndsWith)

- testParseNamespace: "ns|div" returns Evaluator.Tag with colon

Edge case tests:

- testParseEmptyStringThrows: parse("") throws SelectorParseException

- testParseInvalidTokenThrows: parse("??") throws SelectorParseException

- testParseUnclosedAttributeThrows: parse("[href") throws SelectorParseException

- testParseUnclosedPseudoThrows: parse(":lt(") throws SelectorParseException

- testParseInvalidNthThrows: parse(":nth-child(abc)") throws SelectorParseException

- testParseInvalidRegexThrows: parse("[href~=(*]") throws PatternSyntaxException? Actually code compiles Pattern.compile(cq.remainder()), which would throw PatternSyntaxException, but it's not caught, so parse should propagate as IllegalArgumentException? Actually PatternSyntaxException is unchecked. So we can expect PatternSyntaxException.

- testParseInvalidIndexThrows: parse(":eq(notnum)") throws SelectorParseException (due to numeric check)

Potentially also test that whitespace handling works.

Implementation: In each test, call QueryParser.parse(query) and then assertTrue(evaluator instanceof ExpectedClass). For combinators we need to dig deeper: parse returns a CombiningEvaluator.And (or Or). We can assert the outer type and then inner types.

We can also use instanceof to check.

Now produce final test file with markers.

We'll need to import org.jsoup.select.* and org.jsoup.select.Evaluator.* maybe.

Also import java.util.regex.Pattern.

Add @Test(expected=Selector.SelectorParseException.class) for exception tests.

Now produce final answer.
